title: Disney Selling $8 Million Super Bowl Ad Spots Despite Advertiser Pushback

facts.fact: Disney has sold some Super Bowl LXI commercial spots for about $8 million amid pushback from advertisers.
facts.quote: Disney has sold some Super Bowl LXI commercial spots for about $8 million amid pushback from advertisers.

facts.fact: Disney first tried to set a price of $10 million for Super Bowl commercial spots, before lowering to $9 million.
facts.quote: Disney first tried to set a [price of $10 million](https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/disney-10-million-super-bowl-commercials-advertisers-balk-1236723850/), then [$9 million]

facts.fact: Per Variety-sourced reporting, Disney has sold a 'significant chunk' of 30-second Super Bowl spots for about $8 million each.
facts.quote: the company has now sold a “significant chunk” of 30-second spots for about $8 million each.

facts.fact: A source told Variety that Disney has sold 50% of its game-time inventory already.
facts.quote: Still, a source told Variety that Disney has sold 50% of their game-time inventory already.

facts.fact: Disney said advertisers have driven double-digit units at $9 million each from emerging categories.
facts.quote: driving double-digit units at $9 million each in addition to spending across Disney’s football portfolio,

facts.fact: Disney stated that investment is coming from seven major categories, led by A.I., finance, and pharma.
facts.quote: investment coming from seven major categories, led by A.I., finance, and pharma.

facts.fact: The Super Bowl airing on ESPN under the Disney-NFL arrangement is scheduled for February 14, 2027.
facts.quote: their first Super Bowl since 2026 will air on February 14, 2027

facts.fact: Returning Super Bowl advertisers usually get first pick of the next year's spots, a perk Disney reportedly did not offer.
facts.quote: Returning Super Bowl advertisers usually enjoy first pick of the next year’s spots. Disney reportedly didn’t want to offer this perk
